use: Researchers, PhD applicants, research offices and small firms often do not know which UK Research and Innovation (UKRI) council fits an idea, what similar work was funded, or for how much. GtR search and UKRI's Funding Finder do not read the user's abstract; NIH RePORTER Matchmaker does so only for US health research (NIH, 2026); Dimensions is paywalled (Hook et al., 2018); research prototypes classify GtR subjects (Tattershall and Yang, 2017) or map grants across funders (Khor et al., 2018). FundMatch UK takes a title and abstract and returns the likely council with calibrated probabilities and the words behind them, the most similar funded projects, and a typical award range. It does not predict success.
data: All 158,710 Gateway to Research (GtR) projects, joined to 158,710 fund records (amounts, dates) and 97,102 organisations. Input: title and abstract; target: lead funder among eight councils (AHRC, BBSRC, EPSRC, ESRC, Innovate UK, MRC, NERC, STFC). For a cross-country test we also collected 5,000 US and Australian grants.
sufficient: After cleaning, 113,233 projects remain; the smallest class has 5,511 (STFC). Macro-F1 rises from 0.778 with 1,807 training projects to 0.862 with 90,585, and the last doubling adds only 0.9 points (Figure 1): the data is large enough.
ethics: Every record was fetched by our own code from public APIs; no Kaggle or prepared datasets. GtR is under the Open Government Licence v3.0 (credited in the app); NSF data is public domain; NIH's one-request-per-second guidance was respected; ARC data (CC BY-NC-ND 4.0) is used only for non-commercial evaluation. No GtR person records were collected and foreign investigator names were dropped; the app shows no researcher names and stores no user text.
code: collect_gtr.py pages through /projects, /funds and /organisations (100 records per page), waits 1 s between requests, retries 429/5xx errors with exponential back-off and caches every page, so runs resume (Figure 2). The 2026-11-23 run took 32 min for projects and 28 min for funds and survived 26 transient errors. build_dataset.py joins funds to projects through FUNDED links (100% matched); collect_international.py applies the same policy to NSF, NIH and ARC.
prep: Programme budgets (ISCF, GCRF…), which users cannot apply to, were removed, as were placeholders, short texts, boilerplate and joint-grant duplicates (Table 1). Leakage controls: (i) 11% of texts name a funder, so names are masked; on those texts an unmasked model scores 0.929 against 0.887; (ii) grant category and reference reveal the funder ("Collaborative R&D" is 100% Innovate UK), so they are not features; (iii) near-duplicates form 109,104 groups, each kept on one side of the split. Features: TF-IDF uni/bi-grams (min_df 3, max_df 0.5, sublinear, ≤200k features) and frozen 384-d MiniLM and BGE sentence embeddings.
models: This is imbalanced multi-class text classification. Candidates: a majority floor; Complement NB, built for imbalanced text (Rennie et al., 2003); logistic regression and a linear SVM on TF-IDF, strong text classifiers (Joachims, 1998), the former giving probabilities; logistic regression and an MLP on transformer embeddings (Reimers and Gurevych, 2019; Xiao et al., 2023), which capture meaning beyond shared words; and a TF-IDF + BGE ensemble. A CPU-budget SciBERT fine-tune (Beltagy et al., 2019) on 3,000 projects scored 0.784 macro-F1 against 0.825 for TF-IDF + LR on the same rows; a full run needs a GPU.
training: StratifiedGroupKFold gave 90,585 training and 22,648 test projects with no shared group. Hyper-parameters were tuned by macro-F1 in 3-fold group cross-validation on training data with balanced class weights; the test set was used once (Table 2). TF-IDF + LR reached 0.862 macro-F1 with the right council in its top three 99.2% of the time; the SVM tied but gives no probabilities. Embeddings were weaker and the ensemble did not help: councils differ in specific words ("clinical", "crop", "market") that TF-IDF keeps. Per-council F1 is 0.78–0.93; the main confusions (BBSRC/MRC, EPSRC/Innovate UK, AHRC/ESRC; Figure 3) mirror real overlaps. Trained before 2021 and tested after, F1 is 0.827, so yearly retraining is needed.
beyond: Calibration: raw probabilities were slightly over-confident (ECE 0.034; Guo et al., 2017). A temperature (T = 1.13) fitted on out-of-fold training predictions cut ECE to 0.018 without changing any prediction. Explanation: tfidf × coefficient gives each word's exact contribution, shown in the app. Deleting a text's five top words lowered the predicted council's probability by 0.22 and changed 26% of predictions, against 0.01 and 2% for five random words, so explanations are faithful. Transfer: on 3,852 foreign grants mapped to UK councils (Table 3), accuracy falls to 0.67 but top-3 stays at 95%; embeddings transfer slightly better (ensemble 0.70). Search: given 2,000 titles, TF-IDF ranked the project's own abstract among 5,000 in the top 10 for 89.5% (MRR 0.773); hybrid rank fusion (Cormack et al., 2009) reached 92.1% (0.820) but needs PyTorch; BM25 reached 91.6%, SPECTER 75.8%.
deploy: A rule fixed before measuring: peak RAM under 1 GB and p95 latency under 1 s, then the best CV macro-F1 among probabilistic models, preferring a lighter option within 0.01. TF-IDF + LR wins (CV 0.858; Figure 4). The ensemble needs PyTorch, 790 against 370 MB and 190 against 57 ms per query, for no gain; better transfer abroad does not justify exceeding the 690 MB free tier. TF-IDF search is also the most on-topic (P@10 0.350 against 0.330 for BGE), and one vectoriser serves prediction, search and explanation. Awards (MAE in log £, 14,925 test projects): the 30-neighbour median scores 0.836, Ridge on TF-IDF 0.800; LightGBM with council, scheme and duration 0.462, but users rarely know these and its P25–P75 quantiles held only 42% of true awards, against 50% (ideal 50%) for the neighbour band the app keeps.
how: The notebook refits TF-IDF + LR on all 113,233 clean projects and exports NumPy weights (float64 plus an int8 copy), a 64-d int8 SVD index of the abstracts and a metadata table, so the app needs neither the pickle nor PyTorch. src/fundmatch/engine.py rebuilds the vectoriser (Figure 5); a red-team check found and fixed a stop-word mismatch, and logits now match scikit-learn within 1e-5 on 3,070 texts. app.py is the Streamlit UI; the code is on GitHub and Streamlit Community Cloud serves it (Python 3.13, pinned requirements).
showcase: The live app, ScholarPulse UK (Figure 6), was opened on 25 November 2026 with a quantum-control idea. It returned EPSRC at 89% (high confidence: test predictions at or above 0.80 were right 94.3% of the time), a 90% conformal set of EPSRC alone, a novelty band, the words behind the score, Funding Finder links, similar GtR projects, a CPIH-adjustable award band and a trend chart. 61 automated tests pass. The server holds about 616 MiB once loaded but peaks near 819 MiB while starting, above the 690 MB minimum, so memory remains a risk.
limits: The label is the lead funder only, so co-funded work counts as an error; search relevance rests on topic proxies and assistant-drafted labels that the group must still review; a third of projects (mostly studentships) have no award, so some bands rest on few neighbours, and the app warns when fewer than 10 are priced.
